title: In Oklahoma M2.5+ seismicity, ETAS clustering lasted longer at lower background rates, as rate^-0.25 (0.19-0.32), not rate^-1 as rate-and-state theory predicts; it gave no forecast gain
abstract: Question: does the duration of earthquake clustering in Oklahoma induced seismicity change with the local forcing rate, as rate-and-state theory predicts (aftershock duration = A sigma / stressing rate, so duration proportional to background rate^-1)? Approach: we used the ETAS code of an earlier campaign study (OGS catalog, 10,806 M2.5+ targets, 2010-2026, free background per 0.2-degree cell and 6-month bin, tapered Omori kernel exp(-t/tau)). For each parent we computed the background rate of its 3 x 3 cell block in the 6-month bin before its own bin, so that its offspring cannot change it. A new model gives each background quintile its own productivity and a taper tau = tau0 (r/r_ref)^-beta. We tested the method with 7 synthetic catalogs of known beta, repeated the test with time-only, space-only and injection covariates, within periods and magnitude classes and at M3.0+, and made forecasts from fits to 2018 and 2020. Results: over a 36-fold range of background rate, tau fell from 556-611 to 249 days. beta = 0.25 (95% profile interval 0.19-0.32; log-likelihood gain 26.6 for one parameter). beta = 1 was 146.6 log-likelihood units below the maximum. Synthetic catalogs returned beta = -0.05 to 0.04 for true 0, 0.21 for 0.25, 0.48 for 0.5 and 0.79-0.91 for 1. The effect was present in time (study-area rate; gain 36.4 for 4 parameters) and in space (beta = 0.30), with a magnitude control (0.24) and within periods (0.15; tau0 351 days before 2017, 563 after). By period, tau was 560, 333, 646 and 984 days in 2010-2013, 2014-2016, 2017-2019 and 2020-2026. Arbuckle injection volume within 20 km gave no trend. At M3.0+ beta = 0.14 (not clearly different from 0). Forecasts did not improve: from 2019, 1,552 events against 788 observed (one-taper model 1,763); from 2021, 275 against 413 (one-taper model 378). Interpretation: clustering follows the forcing in the direction of rate-and-state theory but much more weakly; if background rate grows as stressing rate^n, n is about 4. Limitations: the background rate is a model estimate from the same catalog; synthetic tests use ETAS itself, not pressure-driven swarms; c and p are shared by groups; one region; network and magnitude-practice changes after 2016.
